readme.summary: Exceptionally clear and thorough documentation with excellent examples and multiple installation paths, though configuration details are minimal since the tool is primarily command-line based.
readme.top_issue: Configuration section could document environment variables, config file options, or alternative trash directory locations if supported

injection_risks.description: The use of os.environ to get the TRASH_PUT_FAKE_UID_FOR_TESTING variable could potentially lead to an injection risk if not properly sanitized.
The Parser class uses argv[0] which is a user-controlled input and could be used for command injection attacks if not properly validated.

critical_findings: Potential command injection risk in the Parser class
Lack of validation on user inputs
security.summary: The trash-cli package has some potential security risks, including command injection and lack of input validation, but overall it appears to be well-structured and secure.

common_complaints: Data loss concerns (files mysteriously deleted from trash)
Permission handling issues (misleading error messages, trashing unremovable files)
Incomplete feature implementations (ZSH completion, restore operation terminating on error)
